study_characteristics.study_objective: Expand and share pre-trained normative models to include surface area and resting-state functional connectivity, and benchmark whether deviation scores from normative models outperform raw features for group differences (schizophrenia vs controls), classification, and prediction of general cognitive ability.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Three benchmarking analyses: (1) Mass univariate group differences (two-sample t-tests with FDR) for SZ vs HC; (2) SVM classification (linear SVC, AUC averaged over 10-fold CV); (3) Regression predicting general cognitive ability using BBS/PC-based linear models in HCP YA.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Normative-model deviation features outperform raw features for SZ vs HC group differences and classification (notably for cortical thickness); regression gains are modest and not statistically significant.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Table 2: Group differences — structural 117/187 significant ROIs with deviation vs 0/187 raw; functional 50/136 vs 0/136 raw. Classification — structural AUC 0.87 (deviation) vs 0.43 (raw), Δ=0.44 (significant); functional AUC 0.69 vs 0.68, Δ=0.01 (ns). Regression (HCP) — structural MSE 0.699 (deviation) vs 0.708 (raw), Δ=-0.008 (ns); functional MSE 0.877 vs 0.890, Δ=-0.013 (ns).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Functional analyses use Yeo-17 parcellation only (Smith-10 shared but not benchmarked); reference cohorts likely overrepresent WEIRD populations; race/ethnicity not modeled; need future expansion to other modalities and higher resolution; broader challenges in brain–behavior reliability.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Pre-trained models are shared with an online portal (pcnportal.dccn.nl) for code-free transfer to new sites; models handle site and QC covariates and demonstrate transfer to unseen clinical and control sites.

general_notes.general_notes: Representative training datasets include ABCD (multiple sites), HCP (YA, Aging, Development), UK Biobank (ukb-11025/11026/11027), OASIS3, CAMCAN, PNC, NKI-RS, TOP, IXI, CNP, and several OpenNeuro datasets (e.g., ds002345, ds002731, SWU_SLIM). See Supplementary files 1–2 for the full site-by-site list with Ns, ages, and sex distributions.
